title: Long-term change within a Neotropical forest: assessing differential functional and floristic responses to disturbance and drought
authors: Enquist, B. J.; Enquist, C. A. F.
summary: Evaluated long-term floristic and functional shifts in a Neotropical forest with emphasis on disturbance and drought context.

title: Long-term shifts in the functional composition and diversity of a tropical dry forest: a 30-yr study
authors: Swenson, N. G.; Hulshof, C. M.; Katabuchi, M.; Enquist, B. J.
summary: Used three censuses across 30 years to quantify population dynamics, species richness, functional diversity, and directional composition change.

title: Remotely sensed assessment of increasing chronic and episodic drought effects on a Costa Rican tropical dry forest
authors: Huang, C.-Y.; Duran, S. M.; Hu, K.-T.; Li, H.-J.; Swenson, N. G.; Enquist, B. J.
summary: Integrated long-term plot observations with satellite metrics to evaluate chronic and episodic drought signals and post-ENSO canopy responses.

title: Improved abundance prediction from presence-absence data
authors: Conlisk, E.; Conlisk, J.; Enquist, B.; Thompson, J.; Harte, J.
summary: Developed improved abundance prediction methods from presence-absence data, relevant to scaling biodiversity inference from sparse observations.

title: Allometric scaling of production and life history variation in vascular plants
authors: Enquist, B. J.; West, G. B.; Charnov, E. L.; Brown, J. H.; Santa, T.; Road, H. P.; Fe, S.; Division, T.; Ms, B.
summary: Classic allometric paper linking plant production and life-history variation to broad scaling relationships.

title: Biodiversity scales from plots to biomes with a universal species-area curve
authors: Harte, J.; Smith, A. B.; Storch, D.
summary: Proposed a universal species-area relationship spanning plots to biomes, useful for framing biodiversity scaling.

title: Foraging by bucket-brigade in leaf-cutter ants
authors: Hubbell, S. P.; Johnson, L. K.; Stanislav, E.; Wilson, B.; Fowler, H.
summary: Described bucket-brigade foraging behavior in leaf-cutter ants, part of the broader ecological context of tropical systems.

title: Interannual variability of growth and reproduction in Bursera simaruba: the role of allometry and resource variability
authors: Hulshof, C. M.; Stegen, J. C.; Swenson, N. G.; Enquist, C. A.; Enquist, B. J.

title: Plant selection and foraging patterns in two species of leaf-cutting ants (Atta)
summary: Analyzed plant selection and foraging patterns in leaf-cutting ants, contributing to dry-forest trophic context.

title: Host-plant selection, diet diversity, and optimal foraging in a tropical leafcutting ant
authors: Rockwood, L. L.; Hubbell, S. P.
summary: Explored host-plant selection and diet diversity in tropical leafcutting ants with an optimal foraging framework.

title: Opposing assembly mechanisms in a neotropical dry forest: implications for phylogenetic and functional community ecology
authors: Swenson, N. G.; Enquist, B. J.
summary: Described opposing assembly mechanisms in a neotropical dry forest, relevant to functional and phylogenetic community ecology.

title: Lianas as structural parasites: the Bursera simaruba example
summary: Used Bursera simaruba to illustrate lianas as structural parasites in tropical forest ecology.

title: The problem and promise of scale dependency in community phylogenetics
authors: Swenson, N. G.; Enquist, B. J.; Pither, J.; Thompson, J.; Zimmerman, J. K.
summary: Discussed how scale dependence affects community phylogenetics and ecological inference.
